_meta.note: These are the 4 cross-cutting strategic risks the team identified. Each is tagged to the markets it applies to so the UI can filter to whichever market is selected. None are engine_reconstruction -- these are verbatim from the deck.
_meta.mitigation_notes: mitigation_notes (added in Round 2) scope each deck mitigation to one market so the selected market never shows another market's rails or partners. They restate the deck mitigation using facts already in markets.json and risks.json -- no new regulatory claims. The cross-cutting 'mitigation' field remains the deck text verbatim.

risks.title: Regulatory Change
risks.subtitle: All three rulebooks are under 18 months old
risks.risk: Brazil's SPSAV regime, Indonesia's POJK 23/2025 track and Dubai's ETD rules are all new; leverage caps can tighten at short notice.
risks.why_it_matters: A cap change or reinterpretation mid-launch forces a product rebuild and a re-filing.
risks.mitigation: Named compliance owner per jurisdiction; monthly regulatory change tracking; pre-filing legal review; design to 5x everywhere so a tighter cap never forces a rebuild.

mitigation_notes.uae: Named VARA compliance owner; monthly tracking of VARA rulebook changes; pre-filing legal review; build to the 5x cap so a tighter cap never forces a rebuild.
mitigation_notes.brazil: Named compliance owner for BCB / CVM; monthly tracking of SPSAV rules and B3 contract classification; pre-filing legal review; build to 5x so a tighter cap never forces a rebuild.
mitigation_notes.indonesia: Named compliance owner for OJK; monthly tracking of the POJK 23/2025 track; pre-filing legal review with the partner; build to 5x so a tighter cap never forces a rebuild.

market_notes.uae: Dubai's ETD rules (VARA Part V, Mar 2026) are months old; a retail leverage cap below 5x would force a product change.
market_notes.brazil: Brazil's SPSAV regime (Res. 519-521/2025) is new and B3's contract classification can still move; leverage caps can tighten at short notice.
market_notes.indonesia: Indonesia's POJK 23/2025 track is new; a reinterpretation mid-launch forces a re-filing through the partner.

risks.title: FX / Capital Controls / Fund Flows
risks.subtitle: Fund flows are three separate problems
risks.risk: Brazil's Res. 521 pulls crypto transfers into FX reporting and requires wallet-owner ID; Indonesia mandates rupiah rails via licensed partners; India's LRS bars margin/derivatives remittance.
risks.why_it_matters: The UPI-first architecture cannot be reused; a wrong fund flow is an offence, not a bug.
risks.mitigation: Local-currency payment rails from day one (Aani, Pix, QRIS/BI-FAST); never route user funds through India; FEMA/LRS home-base review with counsel; KYC, sanctions and transaction monitoring live before launch.

mitigation_notes.uae: Aani rail from day one; never route user funds through India; FEMA/LRS home-base review with counsel; KYC, sanctions and transaction monitoring live before launch.
mitigation_notes.brazil: Pix rail from day one; wallet-owner identification and FX reporting on self-custody transfers (Res. 521); never route user funds through India; FEMA/LRS review with counsel.
mitigation_notes.indonesia: Rupiah rails (QRIS / BI-FAST) through the licensed payment partner from day one; never route user funds through India; FEMA/LRS review with counsel.

market_notes.uae: Dollar-pegged AED and no capital controls, but funds must still never route through India (LRS bars margin/derivatives remittance) — Aani rail from day one.
market_notes.brazil: Res. 521 pulls crypto transfers into FX reporting and requires wallet-owner ID on self-custody transfers; Pix rail from day one.
market_notes.indonesia: Rupiah rails are mandatory via licensed partners (QRIS / BI-FAST); a wrong fund flow is an offence, not a bug.

risks.title: Licensing + Timeline
risks.subtitle: A ~9-month VARA process is the fast case
risks.risk: Dubai's ETD authorisation is sequential to the base licence; Indonesia's Rp100bn trader tier adds a second track; a partner can stall, reprice or lose its licence.
risks.why_it_matters: One slipped approval pushes the whole 18-month plan and the capital behind it.
risks.mitigation: File early for transition-period terms; local licensed partners in Brazil and Indonesia instead of standalone licences; two partners shortlisted per market with exit clauses; checkpoints at months 6, 9 and 12 pause spend.

mitigation_notes.uae: File early for transition-period terms; start the ETD application as soon as the base licence is granted; checkpoints at months 6 and 9 pause spend.
mitigation_notes.brazil: File before the 30 Oct 2026 window closes; enter through a BCB-authorised SPSAV partner rather than a standalone licence; two partners shortlisted with exit clauses; checkpoint at month 12 pauses spend.
mitigation_notes.indonesia: Enter through a licensed Pedagang / PAKD partner instead of the Rp100bn own licence; two partners shortlisted with exit clauses; checkpoint at month 12 pauses spend.

market_notes.uae: ETD authorisation is sequential to the base VARA licence — a ~9-month process is the fast case.
market_notes.brazil: Filing window for existing operators closes 30 Oct 2026; a SPSAV partner can stall, reprice or lose its licence.
market_notes.indonesia: Own Pedagang licence needs Rp100bn capital, so entry depends on a partner that can stall or lose its licence; two partners shortlisted.

risks.title: Reputational / Enforcement
risks.subtitle: One fine becomes every market's headline
risks.risk: CVM ordered a major exchange to stop unauthorised derivatives in Brazil (2020; settled 2024) -- regulators police unlicensed launches, not just disclosure gaps.
risks.why_it_matters: A fine or licence loss in one market taints the other two and the India home base.
risks.mitigation: Launch only after the required authorisation is confirmed, never on another market's approval; identical leverage, margin and liquidation disclosures; segregated client assets and negative-balance protection.

mitigation_notes.uae: No soft launch before ETD authorisation; identical leverage, margin and liquidation disclosures; segregated client assets and negative-balance protection.
mitigation_notes.brazil: Launch only after SPSAV and B3 access are confirmed, never on Dubai's approval; identical disclosures; segregated client assets and negative-balance protection.
mitigation_notes.indonesia: Launch only after the partner route is confirmed; contract terms and a backup partner for partner licence loss; identical disclosures; segregated client assets.

market_notes.brazil: CVM ordered a major exchange to stop unauthorised derivatives (2020; settled 2024) — launching before SPSAV/B3 access is confirmed is exactly the pattern regulators police.
market_notes.uae: VARA publicly names and fines unlicensed operators; no soft launch before ETD authorisation.
market_notes.indonesia: OJK enforces through the licensed partner — a partner losing its licence takes the product offline.

risks.title: No Licensed Route Today
risks.subtitle: The product is either illegal or unlicensable in this market right now
risks.risk: MochaTrade's core product — retail crypto perpetuals funded in local currency — either has no legal basis or cannot be licensed in this market under current rules. Operating anyway risks enforcement action, platform blocks and reputational damage in every other market.
risks.why_it_matters: A fine or block in one market taints the pipeline and the home base. Regulatory blocker markets cannot be unlocked by reweighting the rubric.
risks.mitigation: Do not operate in this market until the specific blocker is lifted. Set a named trigger to revisit (e.g. 'Philippines: BSP lifts VASP moratorium'; 'Turkey: SPK reverses derivatives prohibition'). Aryan to track quarterly.

mitigation_notes.philippines: Trigger: BSP lifts VASP moratorium. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.nigeria: Trigger: SEC digital-asset rules gazetted with a derivatives position. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.pakistan: Trigger: PVARA issues first derivatives licence and publishes final regulations. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.thailand: Trigger: SEC publishes final rules from 2026 consultation with perpetuals/leverage treatment. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.south_africa: Trigger: Capital Flow Management Regulations finalised without the self-custody block, and the ODP capital figure confirmed. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.vietnam: Trigger: Pilot issues first licences and is extended to derivatives at a capital level a minority partner could reach. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.mexico: Trigger: Counsel confirms a lawful route for retail derivatives, or Mexico enacts a crypto-asset licence. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.argentina: Trigger: CNV confirms perpetuals sit inside the PSAV registry (or names the authorisation needed) and corporate FX controls are lifted. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.chile: Trigger: CMF confirms instrument classification of crypto perpetuals and the applicable capital tier. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.colombia: Trigger: Government bill passed with a licence category covering derivatives. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.ghana: Trigger: Licensing window opens after sandbox with published capital and a derivatives position. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.costa_rica: Trigger: Sugef publishes implementing regulations from Decree 10961 addressing derivatives. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.turkey: Trigger: SPK reverses the derivatives prohibition in Communiqué III-35/B.1. Nothing short of that opens this market.
mitigation_notes.malaysia: Trigger: SC permits leveraged or derivative crypto products under a defined retail regime. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.saudi_arabia: Trigger: SAMA/CMA publish a crypto service-provider licensing framework. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.bangladesh: Trigger: Bangladesh Bank withdraws the FERA prohibition and a licensing regime is created. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.egypt: Trigger: CBE publishes a licensing procedure and issues a first licence. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.morocco: Trigger: Bill 42.25 enacted and Office des Changes withdraws the 2017 position. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.oman: Trigger: FSA enacts the Virtual Assets Regulatory Framework with a VASP licence covering derivatives. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.ukraine: Trigger: Draft Law 10225-d passes second reading and is signed, with a licence category for derivatives. Until then, do not operate.
mitigation_notes.sri_lanka: Trigger: SEC-led VASP law enacted and the CBSL banking restriction lifted. Until then, do not operate.

market_notes.philippines: BSP moratorium on new VASP licences; perpetuals have no SEC CASP basis. Actively blocking foreign platforms (Aug 2025 advisory).
market_notes.nigeria: SEC digital-asset rules published for comment Aug 2026 — not yet in force; perpetuals neither permitted nor banned.
market_notes.pakistan: Virtual Assets Act 2026 created PVARA but derivatives licence cohort not yet issued; regime brand new and untested.
market_notes.thailand: SEC recognised crypto as derivatives underlying (Mar 2026) but the perpetuals route depends on a consultation (closed 30 Sep 2026) not yet finalised.
market_notes.south_africa: Crypto derivatives need FSP + ODP (not just CASP); draft Capital Flow Management Regulations (Apr 2026) would block self-custody inflows.
market_notes.vietnam: Pilot requires ~US$380M charter capital, 49% foreign cap, VND-only settlement, spot only. Penalties for unlicensed operations took effect 1 Sep 2026.
market_notes.mexico: Banxico Circular 4/2019 bars banks and ITFs from offering crypto; no exchange licence exists; derivatives rules not found.
market_notes.argentina: CNV PSAV registry silent on derivatives; 'cepo' FX controls constrain settlement.
market_notes.chile: Ley Fintec + CMF NCG 502 cover exchange and custody; whether perpetuals are regulated instruments is unconfirmed.
market_notes.colombia: No licence regime; government bill not yet submitted (Feb 2026).
market_notes.ghana: VASP Act 2025 — no licences yet; sandbox only; operations targeted 2027.
market_notes.costa_rica: Decree 10961 is AML-only; implementing regulations pending; derivatives not addressed.
market_notes.turkey: Leveraged trading, derivatives and margin in crypto expressly prohibited (Communiqué III-35/B.1). Core product is unlawful.
market_notes.malaysia: SC clarification (Jan 2026) bars CMSL holders from margin and lending; cash-upfront only. No retail-perps route.
market_notes.saudi_arabia: 2018 Standing Committee declared virtual currencies unauthorised; no crypto-exchange or derivatives licence exists.
market_notes.bangladesh: All crypto transactions breach FERA 1947; ban reiterated as recently as Sep 2025; no exceptions.
market_notes.egypt: Article 206 of Law 194/2020 prohibits trading without CBE approval; no licence has ever been issued; penalties include imprisonment.
market_notes.morocco: 2017 joint ban (Office des Changes + BAM + AMMC) still in force; Bill 42.25 under review, no parliamentary date.
market_notes.oman: AML registration only (FSA E/35/2023); no licence categories, fees or capital yet published.
market_notes.ukraine: Draft Law 10225-d passed first reading (Sep 2025); not enacted; wartime currency restrictions on top.
market_notes.sri_lanka: Cabinet approved VASP drafting (28 Jul 2026) but crypto stays outside the regulated system; CBSL banking restriction in force.

risks.title: Partner / Single Point of Failure
risks.subtitle: Entry depends on a third party that can stall, reprice or lose its licence
risks.risk: Where MochaTrade cannot operate standalone — because local entity requirements, capital thresholds or partner-fronted onboarding are mandatory — the launch depends on a licensed local partner. That partner can stall, reprice or lose its own licence mid-launch.
risks.why_it_matters: A single partner failure stalls the entire market entry and puts capital at risk. Regulatory markets move faster than partner negotiations.
risks.mitigation: Two partners shortlisted per market with exit clauses; clear SLA and fallback triggers in the contract; milestone checkpoints pause spend if partner progress stalls.

mitigation_notes.el_salvador: CNAD DASP registration is standalone at low capital (~US$5k fee); partner risk is low but US-equities and rail access may still need a local bank relationship.
mitigation_notes.kazakhstan: AIFC entity with substance required; two AFSA-licensed partners shortlisted; exit clauses and backup partner.
mitigation_notes.kenya: Entry via licensed payments partner (M-Pesa/PesaLink access); two partners shortlisted; FATF grey-list banking friction is the secondary risk.
mitigation_notes.bahrain: CBB Cat 3/4 licence own or via partner; derivatives need separate CBB approval — two routes, two partner tracks.
mitigation_notes.peru: No crypto licence; AML registration via local entity or branch; local payment acquirer for Yape/Plin; low partner dependency.
mitigation_notes.uruguay: BCU PSAV licence needs local entity; no evidence of direct foreign rail access; partner or branch required.
mitigation_notes.georgia: NBG VASP registration needs officer in Georgia ≥14 days/month; banking access is described as the bottleneck.
mitigation_notes.mauritius: FSC licence needs Mauritius office and two resident directors — substance-heavy; rail unverified.
mitigation_notes.panama: No licence exists; entry would depend on a legal structure to be confirmed once Draft Law 314 passes.
mitigation_notes.philippines: Any future entry would be partner-fronted (BSP supervised bank/EMI); partner risk is secondary to the current licence block.
mitigation_notes.nigeria: Resident CEO required in the draft rules; local partner essential; secondary risk once rules are in force.
mitigation_notes.pakistan: Track B NOC needs Pakistan-registered company; SBP bank accounts only for licensed VASPs; partner or local entity.
mitigation_notes.thailand: Thai limited company required for every licence category; no standalone foreign-entity route.
mitigation_notes.south_africa: Local Pty entity, two experienced directors, FSP + ODP two-track; substance-heavy.
mitigation_notes.mexico: Bank/ITF partner required for peso rails; standalone foreign-operator rail access is blocked.
mitigation_notes.argentina: Local SA/SRL or branch 5–8 months; FX controls constrain partner settlement.
mitigation_notes.chile: Foreign rail access has limited evidence; local bank or PSP partner likely required.
mitigation_notes.colombia: No licence; any future entry depends on the SFC bill and a licensed partner.
mitigation_notes.ghana: SEC (exchanges/brokerage) + BoG (custody/payments) dual track; two-partner structure.
mitigation_notes.costa_rica: Licensed bank/partner required for SINPE Móvil access.
mitigation_notes.malaysia: Local company required; DAX licence + bank partners for rail access.

risks.title: Derivatives Product Gap
risks.subtitle: Retail perpetuals are the exception, not the rule, globally
risks.risk: Most jurisdictions have not yet said whether retail crypto perpetuals are a permitted financial product. Even markets where crypto is legal often require a separate derivatives authorisation, and regulators have moved to restrict retail leverage globally.
risks.why_it_matters: Launching before the derivatives question is settled creates enforcement risk; a product rebuild mid-launch is costly.
risks.mitigation: Obtain local counsel opinion on derivatives classification before filing. Budget for a spot-only fallback if perpetuals cannot be authorised. Tag every market note with a 'derivatives position' confidence score.

mitigation_notes.el_salvador: Derivatives/leverage route unverified; obtain CNAD counsel opinion before launch. Spot-only fallback available.
mitigation_notes.kazakhstan: AIFC rules contemplate digital-asset derivatives under AFSA approval; retail perps/leverage cap unconfirmed — AFSA pre-application meeting recommended.
mitigation_notes.kenya: Derivatives/margin/leverage not addressed in VASP Act 23 or Regulations 134; obtain CMA counsel opinion.
mitigation_notes.bahrain: CBB requires separate approval for derivatives with a derivatives risk framework — this is a second licensing track.
mitigation_notes.peru: No leverage cap found; SMV/SBS say they lack jurisdiction over crypto; obtain SBS/SMV counsel opinion.
mitigation_notes.uruguay: Covered services (Circular 2507): exchange, VA-to-VA trading, custody, transfers — perpetuals not addressed.
mitigation_notes.georgia: No derivatives or leverage provisions in NBG registration rules; VA lending and VA payments also restricted.
mitigation_notes.mauritius: No FSC leverage cap found; retail-perpetual treatment and non-resident retail servicing are unclear.
mitigation_notes.panama: No explicit derivatives rules; perpetuals are a grey zone until Draft Law 314 passes.
mitigation_notes.philippines: SEC CASP rules silent on derivatives; no retail leverage cap published.
mitigation_notes.nigeria: Draft SEC rules neither permit nor ban perpetuals; no leverage cap.
mitigation_notes.pakistan: PVARA regulations in consultation; no confirmed treatment of derivatives or retail leverage.
mitigation_notes.thailand: Perpetual eligibility depends on final rules from the Aug 2026 SEC consultation — not yet published.
mitigation_notes.south_africa: Retail leverage cap not found; crypto derivatives classified as securities under FMA — FSP + ODP needed.
mitigation_notes.argentina: RG 1058/2025 silent on derivatives; perpetuals may need a separate CNV derivatives authorisation.
mitigation_notes.chile: Whether derivatives are regulated instruments under Ley Fintec is unconfirmed.
